skill.name: neovim-debugging
skill.description: Diagnose Neovim and LazyVim errors, broken keymaps, plugin failures, LSP issues, visual defects, and performance problems through targeted hypothesis testing.
skill.summary: Find Neovim configuration causes with focused tests and evidence-based fixes.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

security_audit.summary: Most matches are scanner false positives caused by Neovim terms, Markdown fences, local configuration paths, and headless diagnostic commands. Fixed filenames under /tmp create symlink and log-disclosure risks, while executable templates can become injection vectors if placeholders contain untrusted input. Publication should wait until command templates and temporary-file handling are hardened.

remediation.issue: Executable shell and Lua templates accept unspecified placeholder values.
remediation.suggestion: Validate plugin, module, and configuration identifiers with strict allowlists before execution. Never interpolate user text into shell or Lua command strings.

remediation.issue: Diagnostic commands write logs to predictable shared /tmp paths.
remediation.suggestion: Create private temporary files with mktemp, set restrictive permissions, pass the generated path safely, and remove files after diagnosis.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Placeholders in Executable Commands
semantic_findings.description: The skill encourages headless execution with PLUGIN_NAME, CONFIG_PATH, and MODULE inside a double-quoted shell argument. Untrusted substitutions can trigger shell expansion or execute arbitrary Lua.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The executable templates and placeholders are explicit, and no validation or safe argument-passing rule is provided. Exploitation still depends on unsafe substitution by the agent.

content.value_statement: Neovim configuration failures are difficult to isolate across plugins, mappings, and runtime state. This skill applies targeted tests to identify causes and propose verified fixes.
actual_capabilities: Classifies errors, keymap failures, plugin loading issues, performance problems, and visual defects.
Forms ordered hypotheses and selects focused tests for each symptom.
Uses headless Neovim checks to inspect options, modules, mappings, and plugin state.
Explains common Lua, LSP, Treesitter, Telescope, which-key, and completion errors.
Produces a diagnosis with root cause, evidence, solution, and prevention guidance.
limitations: Requires Neovim and relevant plugins to be installed in the working environment.
Cannot confirm visual or intermittent behavior without user feedback.
Examples focus on LazyVim, lazy.nvim, and several common plugins.
Shell commands and local configuration reads require user approval and careful input validation.

use_cases.title: Repair a Broken Keymap
use_cases.description: Trace missing or conflicting mappings, leader settings, plugin loading, and which-key triggers.

use_cases.title: Investigate Plugin Failures
use_cases.description: Check plugin installation, load conditions, exported functions, configuration calls, and version changes.

use_cases.title: Profile Editor Performance
use_cases.description: Separate startup and runtime delays, collect timing evidence, and identify slow plugins or functions.

prompt_templates.title: Explain an Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this Neovim error: [complete error]. Explain its likely cause and give one focused verification step.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Keymap
prompt_templates.prompt: My Neovim key [key] should [expected behavior], but [actual behavior]. Build a short hypothesis list and test the most likely cause first.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate why [plugin] is not working in [Neovim or LazyVim]. Use this configuration and error evidence: [details]. Confirm loading before proposing changes.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this Neovim performance problem: [symptom and trigger]. Design a minimal comparison, interpret the measurements, and identify the strongest root-cause evidence.

output_examples.input: The local leader mappings exist, but which-key does not open for the local leader.
output_examples.output: Diagnosis: which-key is loaded, but its automatic trigger excludes the local leader. Verify manual opening, then add the local leader trigger.

output_examples.input: A Telescope function became unavailable after updating plugins.
output_examples.output: Diagnosis: the update likely changed an exported API or extension load order. Confirm the function and locked versions before changing configuration.

output_examples.input: Neovim startup is slow, but a minimal configuration starts quickly.
output_examples.output: Diagnosis: plugin or user configuration overhead is the likely source. Compare timing entries and test the slowest component in isolation.

best_practices: Provide the complete error, exact trigger, expected behavior, and recent configuration changes.
Run the smallest diagnostic that can distinguish between the leading hypotheses.
Review commands, validate placeholders, and protect diagnostic logs before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not run every diagnostic command without a specific hypothesis.
Do not interpolate untrusted names or expressions into shell or Lua commands.
Do not modify configuration until evidence identifies the responsible layer.

faq.question: Does this skill support standard Neovim?
faq.answer: Yes. Core error, keymap, LSP, UI, and performance methods apply without LazyVim.

faq.question: Does it edit my configuration automatically?
faq.answer: It can propose changes, but configuration edits should follow a confirmed diagnosis and user approval.

faq.question: Can it debug visual problems?
faq.answer: It can inspect relevant settings and plugins. User feedback is still needed for appearance and interactive behavior.

faq.question: Which plugins receive specific guidance?
faq.answer: The references cover lazy.nvim, which-key, LSP, Treesitter, Telescope, nvim-cmp, Snacks, and LazyVim.

faq.question: Why does it use headless Neovim?
faq.answer: Headless checks provide repeatable evidence about modules, options, mappings, and plugin state without opening the interface.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the full error, exact reproduction steps, expected result, actual result, versions, and recent changes.
